headline: High: aci’s broad egress plus dexter’s autonomous execution and file/API access create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and cascading actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP/direct function calls and broad egress, while dexter runs autonomously and can read/write its scratchpad. If aci’s outputs are copied into dexter inputs or shared files, attacker-controlled content could steer tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF aci output is pasted into dexter prompts or scratchpad files
IF both agents share a workspace or message queue without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate their workspaces and scratchpads
Disable copy-paste handoff between agents
Add a provenance header to every transferred artifact
Review any tool-call text before dexter executes it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and customer support data and has broad network egress; dexter touches financial and market data and sends requests to multiple third-party APIs. If they share files or credentials, sensitive data from either side can be exposed externally. The pair’s default networked behavior makes leakage materially plausible.
conditions: IF aci and dexter share any workspace, secrets store, or OAuth principal
IF either agent forwards shared files or context to its external APIs
mitigations: Use separate API keys and OAuth principals
Keep shared data out of both agents’ default directories
Turn off automatic file attachment to API calls
Redact CRM and financial fields before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have broad network egress; dexter also writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. If they operate on the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or overlapping API actions can race or overwrite state. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible rather than blocked.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or scratchpad
IF both agents mutate the same external API records without coordination
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and accounts
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run lock
Avoid concurrent edits to shared CRM or research records
Check for last-write-wins conflicts before syncing
requires-engineering: add transactional locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and dexter is autonomous with access to external APIs. If aci’s outputs are treated as authoritative by dexter, errors can cascade into downstream actions such as sending messages or making API-backed decisions. No verification step is documented, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF dexter consumes aci-produced text or structured outputs as input
IF dexter executes actions without an independent verification step
mitigations: Require human review before any outbound action
Insert a validation step between agents
Limit dexter to read-only mode for aci-derived inputs
Log and diff every transformed field before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation and policy checks before tool calls

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and customer support data, while dexter handles financial data and market data and sends it to third-party APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention, residency, and regulated data handling if the same records are shared across both systems. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer or financial records are shared between the agents
IF retention or residency policies differ across the APIs they call
mitigations: Classify shared data before transfer
Keep regulated records out of dexter’s API calls
Review retention settings on all external services
Document a data-processing agreement for shared workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
